title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: US disables ship defying Iran blockade
preheader: Tehran vows to keep the Strait of Hormuz shut and break the US embargo.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Saturday, November 28, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 5 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: US disables ship trying to break Iran blockade
stories.why_important: The US military disabled a commercial ship as it tried to leave Iran through a blockade. An adviser to Iran's supreme leader said Tehran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut. The standoff risks a wider Gulf conflict and threatens global oil shipping.
stories.what_overlooked: The ship was disabled in the Gulf of Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz itself. That shows the US blockade now reaches beyond the narrow waterway of Hormuz.
stories.prediction: Check whether Iran's navy escorts a second ship through the blockade, as success would show Tehran can challenge US enforcement.

stories.story_title: Hackers breach US Air Force Cloud One platform
stories.why_important: Hackers reportedly broke into Cloud One, the Air Force's main cloud system, and reached air-defense radar and munitions tracking data. The Pentagon says its networks are secure but did not deny the breach, and that raises questions about US military cyber defenses.
stories.what_overlooked: Cloud One gathers data from more than 200 Air Force sites worldwide. The reported breach could expose supply and personnel records, not just radar feeds.
stories.prediction: See whether the Pentagon confirms the breach or names the hackers, since formal naming would turn this into a major cyber-diplomacy fight.

stories.story_title: Taiwan votes in local elections as China sends warplanes
stories.why_important: Taiwan holds local elections on Saturday, and the Taipei mayor's race is the main contest. China has sent warplanes and criticized a Taipei candidate, while local campaigns have focused on transport and childcare. The results will test support for parties before the 2028 presidential vote.
stories.what_overlooked: Daily Maverick says the China issue has not played a big part in campaigns. Beijing's warplanes may be trying to sway a race where voters focus elsewhere.
stories.prediction: Track Taipei's mayoral result and whether China sends more warplanes around the island after polls close; a close race could reshape 2028.

quick_hits.text: Spain holds a snap general election this weekend, with polls suggesting Pedro Sánchez's Socialists may lose to a PP-Vox right-wing bloc.
Russia's Putin commissioned the nuclear submarine Perm into the Pacific Fleet, calling it a major event for Russia's nuclear deterrent.
Thomas Lubanga, the ICC's first convicted child-soldier recruiter, is leading a new rebel offensive toward Bunia in eastern Congo.
Zelensky said Trump calling Putin a 'friend' was like calling Hitler a friend in World War II.
The US military used counter-drone technology to repel about six drones swarming RAF Lakenheath this month, with Iran suspected, the FT reported.

big_number.context: A Sberbank study says AI could replace 13% of Russian workers, mainly office and retail staff, saving wages and making managers more productive.
